newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle end mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle end mixed.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures ended mixed after a light trading session, traders said.

December live cattle showed support from short covering promoted by the current large discount to cash. However, prices slipped from best levels by the close as the market continued to show overhead pressure from projections of increased cattle numbers going into December, traders said.
Fed cattle supplies were expected to rise and beef prices to decline in December, partly from a seasonal trend for reduced beef demand, they said.

Prudential Securities notably bought December late while Rosenthal Collins and R.J. O'Brien spread long August/short April. Rosenthal Collins and E.D.& F. Man notably sold early while R.J. O'Brien, ADM Investor Services and RBH bought. Cargill Investor Services notably sold February and Refco spread long February/short December late, pit sources said.
Live cattle closed 0.150 cent higher to 0.050 lower with December up most at 66.725 cents.

In live cattle options, RBH actively sold April 64 puts early. Volatility in December was under pressure while February was firm. There was some buying of the February strangle late, buying 75 puts and selling 80 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures found some support around noon on short covering, but slipped late on selling by LFG and closing sell stops. R.J. O'Brien also sold on the local short covering rally to weigh on sentiment, traders said.
Much of the pressure in feeders came from higher corn futures which offset a rising index and recovery in deferred live cattle futures late, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.18 to $63.48 per cwt.

Cargill Investor Services spread long October live cattle/short May feeders and long June cattle/short April feeders. ADM Investor Services and LIT division of First Options spread long March/short November feeders, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle ended 0.175 cent lower to 0.175 higher with November off most at 64.575 cents.
